title: _IN_FLIGHT_RESERVATIONS stores (profile, reservation_bytes, operation) tuples but only reservation_bytes is ever read; profile and operation are never consumed
description: The process-wide ledger `_IN_FLIGHT_RESERVATIONS: dict[int, tuple[ExecutionProfile, int, str]]` is written at line 525 with `(profile, reservation_bytes, operation)`, but the only read site (line 512) destructures and uses solely the middle `amount` (`sum(amount for _profile, amount, _operation in ...)`). The `profile` and `operation` fields are never surfaced anywhere: the ExecutionAdmissionError for `in_flight_memory_budget_exceeded` reports only the aggregate `reserved` sum and the `limit_bytes`, not a per-reservation breakdown by profile/operation. The ledger value could be just the int `reservation_bytes`, simplifying the type and the write. (The repro at review/02-findings/repro likewise reads only `amount`.)
evidence: Grep for _IN_FLIGHT_RESERVATIONS across the repo (*.py) shows exactly: declaration (line 209), read at line 512 `sum(amount for _profile, amount, _operation in _IN_FLIGHT_RESERVATIONS.values())`, write at line 525, pop at line 541, clear at line 561. The two underscore-prefixed binders (`_profile`, `_operation`) at the only read site confirm those tuple fields are intentionally discarded; no other code path reads them.
behavior_preservation: Storing `reservation_bytes` directly as the dict value (or keeping the tuple but documenting it as reserved-for-diagnostics) produces identical admission decisions, since only the summed amount is read. No externally observable behavior depends on the stored profile/operation.
est_reduction: -2 fields of stored state per reservation; simpler ledger value type
